origin: cwe/94/csharp Taint Sinks: CSharpScript.EvaluateAsync() with user input

finding.name: Improper Control of Generation of Code
finding.summary: A request-supplied formula expression is evaluated with Roslyn CSharpScript using imports and references that expose the application runtime.

trap: Removing System.IO from imports, filtering obvious method names, or assuming ScriptOptions.WithReferences confines what the script can do. Roslyn scripting is not a sandbox; the fix should replace runtime compilation with fixed operations or a purpose-built restricted evaluator.
must_preserve: Approved invoice formula previews still return a value in the same JSON shape, but arbitrary C# code, reflection, file, process, and environment access are not evaluated in-process.
